# MOS Documentation

> MOS (Modular Operating System) is a lightweight, web-based management system for servers and homelabs, built on Devuan Linux.

This is the official documentation for MOS. It covers installation, storage pools, shares, Docker, LXC, virtual machines, networking, the MOS Hub, plugins and the MOS API.

- [Full documentation (single file)](https://docs.mos-official.net/llms-full.txt)

## Documentation

- [Welcome to MOS-Docs](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/): MOS is a lightweight, Devuan-based OS for server and homelab management with Docker, LXC, VMs, storage pools, shares, monitoring, notifications, REST API, and plugins. Open source, no telemetry.

### Installation

- [Create Bootable Media](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Installation/Create-Bootable-Media): Create a bootable USB stick or VM image to install MOS (Modular Operating System) on your server or homelab.
- [First Walkthrough](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Installation/First-Walkthrough): Complete the MOS first walkthrough: set root password, configure web login, network, storage, and system settings.
- [Testing MOS in a Virtual Machine](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Installation/Testing-MOS-in-a-Virtual-Machine): Test MOS (Modular Operating System) in a virtual machine before installing on physical hardware. Step-by-step QEMU/KVM and VirtualBox guide.
- [ARM Support (Experimental)](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Installation/ARM-Support): Install MOS on ARM devices like Orange Pi and Raspberry Pi. Experimental ARM64 support guide with kernel and DTB configuration.

### Dashboard

- [WebUI Overview](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Dashboard/WebUI-Overview): Overview of the MOS web interface: dashboard, navigation menu, storage, virtualization, and system configuration panels explained.

### Disks

- [S.M.A.R.T.](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Disks/SMART): Configure S.M.A.R.T. monitoring in MOS to track disk health, temperature thresholds, and receive warnings for HDD, SSD, and NVMe drives.

### Pools

- [Create a Storage Pool](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Pools/Create-Storage-Pool): Create and configure storage pools in MOS using mergerfs, SnapRAID, Btrfs, or ZFS. Step-by-step guide with pool types and filesystem options.
- [Virtual Pools](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Pools/Virtual-Pools): Combine existing storage paths into a single virtual pool using mergerfs, without requiring dedicated physical disks.
- [ZFS](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Pools/ZFS): Enable ZFS support in MOS via the OpenZFS Driver plugin. CLI-only ZFS pool management with automatic import on boot.

### Shares

- [Create the First Shares](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Shares/Create-the-First-Shares): Create network shares in MOS with SMB and NFS. Configure share permissions, access control, and storage pool assignment.

### MOS Hub

- [MOS Hub Settings](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/MOS-Hub/MOS-Hub-Settings): Configure the MOS Hub settings: enable/disable the app store, control update behavior, and manage template repositories.
- [Creating Your Own MOS Hub Repository](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/MOS-Hub/Creating-Your-Own-MOS-Hub-Repository): Create your own MOS Hub repository on GitHub to share Docker templates, Compose templates, and plugins with the MOS community.

### Docker

- [Docker Service](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Docker/Docker-Service): Configure the Docker service in MOS: enable Docker, set storage locations, configure networking, and manage update checks.
- [Start the First Container](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Docker/Start-the-First-Container): Deploy your first Docker container in MOS using the Docker service or MOS Hub templates. Complete setup guide with networking and volume configuration.

### LXC

- [Container Overview](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/LXC/LXC-Overview): Overview of the LXC container list in MOS: columns, container states, storage usage and management actions.
- [LXC Service](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/LXC/LXC-Service): Configure the LXC service in MOS: enable Linux Containers, set storage locations, and manage container networking.

### VMs

- [VM Service](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/VMs/VM-Service): Configure the VM service in MOS: enable KVM/QEMU virtual machines and define storage locations for VM data.
- [Create the First VM](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/VMs/Create-the-First-VM): Create your first virtual machine in MOS with KVM/QEMU. Configure CPU, memory, storage, network, and boot from ISO images.

### Plugins & Drivers

- [MOS Backup Plugin](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Plugins/MOS-Backup-Plugin): MOS Backup Plugin: Backup and restore your MOS system with this plugin.
- [Drivers](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Plugins/Drivers): Manage hardware drivers in MOS via Driver Plugins from the MOS Hub. Install NVIDIA, DVB, and other kernel module drivers.
- [MOS Plugin Development Guide](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Plugins/MOS-Plugin-Development-Guide): Develop your own MOS plugin: Vue-based configuration pages, bash functions, plugin settings, and GitHub Actions build workflow.

### Terminal

- [Terminal](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Terminal/): Access the MOS system shell directly from the browser with the Web Terminal.

### Filebrowser

- [Filebrowser](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Filebrowser/): Overview of the MOS Filebrowser: web-based file manager for browsing, navigating, and inspecting the entire file system of your MOS server directly from the WebUI.

### Settings


#### System

- [Update System](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/System/Update-System): Update MOS firmware and kernel: choose update channels (alpha, beta, stable), select releases, and manage kernel updates.

#### System Configuration

- [Users](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/User-Management/Users): Create and manage user accounts in MOS: assign roles, configure Samba access, and control permissions for shares and services.
- [System](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/System-Configuration/System): Configure MOS system settings: hostname, keymap, timezone, CPU governor, swap, zswap, NTP, proxy, and display options.
- [Cron Jobs](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/System-Configuration/Cron-Jobs): Create and manage cron jobs in MOS: schedule automated tasks, backups, log rotation, and custom scripts with flexible timing.
- [Logs](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/System-Configuration/Logs): View and browse system log files in MOS: access API, boot, cron, Docker, and syslog entries through the WebUI log viewer.
- [Notifications](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/System-Configuration/Notifications): Configure notification providers in MOS to receive system alerts via Email, Discord, Gotify, Pushbits, or custom webhook providers.
- [User Profile](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/User-Management/User-Profile): Configure user profile settings in MOS: interface preferences, language, dark mode, UI color, and MFA/TOTP two-factor authentication.

#### Hardware

- [Boot](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Hardware/Boot): Install and manage the MOS bootloader: install to disk, configure boot files, and set up extra partitions for storage pools.
- [USB Devices](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Hardware/USB-Devices): Overview of USB devices connected to the MOS system, including vendor IDs, product IDs, and bus information.
- [PCI Devices](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Hardware/PCI-Devices): Overview of PCI devices detected on the MOS system, including slot information, device classes, and vendor/device IDs.
- [ZRAM](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Hardware/ZRAM): Configure ZRAM compressed swap and RAM disks on MOS to maximize memory efficiency on systems with limited RAM.
- [Sensors](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Hardware/Sensors): Monitor hardware sensors in MOS: display temperatures, voltages, fan speeds, and custom metrics on the dashboard.

#### Network

- [Network Interfaces](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Network/Network-Configuration): Configure network interfaces in MOS: ethernet, bridged, and bond modes, static IP, DHCP, VLAN, and IPv6 support with 60-second rollback protection.
- [Network Services](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Network/Network-Services): Enable network services in MOS: SSH, NFS, Samba, Rsync, Remote Mounting, Dnsmasq, NUT (UPS), Tailscale, and Netbird for remote access, file sharing, and VPN connectivity.
- [iSCSI Target](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Network/iSCSI-Target): Configure iSCSI targets on MOS to share block storage over the network using the iSCSI protocol.
- [iSCSI Initiator](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Network/iSCSI-Initiator): Configure the iSCSI Initiator on MOS to connect to remote iSCSI targets and mount their block storage locally.
- [Network Ports](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Network/Network-Ports): Network ports used by MOS: WebUI (80), API (998), Notify (999), VNC consoles (5900+), and DNS (53). Configure firewalls and reverse proxies correctly.
- [Token](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Settings/Network/Token): Manage authentication tokens in MOS: create MOS Admin API tokens, GitHub tokens, and Docker Hub tokens for extended functionality.

### API

- [MOS API Overview](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/API/MOS-API-Overview): MOS REST API overview: fully documented API used by the WebUI. Automate, script, and integrate MOS with external tools via Bearer Token authentication.
- [API Reference](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/API/API-Reference): Interactive reference for the MOS REST API: browse every endpoint by category, expand to see parameters, request/response schemas and copy-ready example requests.
- [Rate Limits](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/API/Rate-Limits): MOS API rate limits configuration: general request limits and login brute-force protection via environment variables.

### Advanced Usage

- [System Architecture](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/System-Architecture): MOS system architecture: runs entirely in RAM from a USB stick with persistent storage for configuration. Understand the lightweight, energy-efficient design for homelabs.
- [Docker Local Host Access](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/Docker-Local-Host-Access-Shim): Enable Docker containers on LAN networks (macvlan/ipvlan) to access the MOS host system via a shim interface plugin.
- [Disable MD5 Verification](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/Disable-MD5-Verification): Disable MD5 checksum verification on MOS boot for advanced scenarios. Marker file-based configuration.
- [Persistent Package Installation](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/Persistent-Package-Installation): Install persistent Debian packages on MOS that survive reboots. Place .deb files in /boot/optional/packages for automatic installation.
- [Kernel Module Configuration](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/Kernel-Module-Configuration): Configure persistent kernel module parameters in MOS via custom modprobe.d files. Useful for ARM board-specific driver settings.
- [Bash Profile Configuration](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/Bash-Profile-Configuration): Customize your MOS SSH session with a persistent .bash_profile: aliases, environment variables, prompt colors, and custom functions.

#### System Startup

- [Early Boot Script](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/System-Startup/Early-Boot-Script): MOS Early Boot Script (boot.sh): the earliest execution point for deep system-level modifications before drivers, network, and storage are loaded.
- [Pre-Start Script](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/System-Startup/Pre-Start-Script): MOS Pre-Start Script (pre-start.sh): execute commands before storage pools are mounted and services are started.
- [Mounted Script](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/System-Startup/Mounted-Script): MOS Mounted Script (mounted.sh): execute commands after storage pools are mounted but before services start.
- [Post-Start Script](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/System-Startup/Post-Start-Script): MOS Post-Start Script (post-start.sh): execute commands after all services are fully started.
- [Pool Mount Scripts](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Advanced-Usage/System-Startup/Pool-Mount-Scripts): MOS Pool Mount Scripts: execute custom scripts when specific storage pools are mounted during boot.

### Troubleshooting

- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Troubleshooting/): MOS troubleshooting guide: common issues and solutions for boot problems, network configuration, Docker, LXC, and pool recovery.
- [Diagnostics](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Troubleshooting/Diagnostics): Create a MOS diagnostics archive: collect system information, logs, and configuration for troubleshooting and community support.

### Support MOS

- [Support MOS](https://docs.mos-official.net/docs/Support-MOS/Support_MOS): Support the MOS project: donate to help continued development of the free and open-source Modular Operating System.

## Glossary

- **API Token**: A token created under Settings > Network > Token that authenticates requests to the MOS API from outside the WebUI.
- **Appdata**: The directory where Docker containers keep their persistent configuration and data. It must live on a storage pool and should be backed up regularly.
- **bcachefs**: A copy-on-write filesystem with checksums and optional replication, available as a MOS pool type.
- **Bond**: Combines two or more physical network interfaces into one logical interface for redundancy or throughput. The switch must be configured to match (LACP or static).
- **Boot device**: The USB stick or internal disk MOS boots from. Persistent system configuration lives in /boot/config on this device.
- **Bridge**: A virtual network switch that connects virtual machines and containers to the physical LAN. The recommended interface type for most MOS installations.
- **Btrfs**: A copy-on-write Linux filesystem with snapshots and checksums. Can be used as a pool filesystem and is required for snapshot-based LXC backups.
- **CHAP**: Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol. Used to authenticate an iSCSI initiator against a target.
- **Diagnostics**: A downloadable .tar.gz archive containing system information, logs and configuration. Attach it when asking for support.
- **Dnsmasq**: A lightweight DNS forwarder and DHCP server that MOS can enable for the local network.
- **Docker**: The container runtime MOS uses for applications. It is enabled and configured under Settings > Virtualization > Docker Service.
- **Docker Compose**: A multi-container stack defined in a compose.yaml file. MOS Hub can deploy Compose stacks as a single app.
- **Docker Template**: A JSON file describing a container (image, ports, volumes, environment). MOS saves one automatically for every container you create.
- **Firmware**: In MOS, the complete system image including the OS and kernel that is installed on the boot device and updated through Settings > System > Update System.
- **FSNavigator**: Internal name of the Filebrowser service. The WebUI calls it Filebrowser; the API endpoints use fsnavigator.
- **Hub Repository**: A GitHub repository in the layout the MOS Hub expects (docker/, compose/, plugins/) that can be added as a template source.
- **iSCSI**: A protocol that shares block storage over the network. MOS can export storage as a target and mount remote targets as an initiator.
- **IQN**: The unique identifier of an iSCSI target or initiator. The initiator IQN is generated automatically by MOS.
- **KVM/QEMU**: The full-virtualization stack used for MOS virtual machines. VMs are enabled under Settings > Virtualization > VM Service.
- **LUN**: A block device exported by an iSCSI target. Each LUN is backed by a disk, partition or image file on the MOS server.
- **LXC**: Lightweight OS-level virtualization that shares the host kernel. Containers are managed on the LXC page and enabled under Settings > Virtualization > LXC Service.
- **mergerfs**: A union filesystem that combines several disks into one mountpoint. Often combined with SnapRAID.
- **MFA**: Multi-factor authentication using a TOTP app in addition to the password. Each account also gets recovery codes for when the app is unavailable.
- **Minimal Free Space**: The free-space threshold at which MOS stops writing to a disk and moves on to the next disk in a mergerfs or nonraid pool.
- **MOS API**: The REST API used by the WebUI and available for automation. Interactive documentation (Swagger UI) is served at /api-docs/ on the MOS IP.
- **MOS Hub**: MOS app catalog for installing Docker containers, Compose stacks and plugins.
- **Netbird**: An open-source mesh VPN based on WireGuard that MOS can enable as an alternative to Tailscale.
- **NFS**: The file-sharing protocol used to mount MOS shares on Linux and Unix clients.
- **nonraid**: A pool type with dedicated parity disks, similar to Unraid. Requires the nonraid driver, which is installed from the MOS Hub.
- **NUT**: The service MOS uses to monitor a UPS and trigger a graceful shutdown when mains power is lost.
- **OVMF**: The UEFI firmware used by virtual machines. Required for Windows 11 and modern Linux distributions.
- **Parity**: Redundant data stored on one or more parity disks so a failed data disk can be rebuilt. Parity disks hold no usable capacity. Used by SnapRAID and nonraid.
- **PCI Passthrough**: Giving a virtual machine exclusive access to a physical PCI device such as a GPU or controller. The host cannot use the device while the VM runs.
- **Plugin**: An installable extension from the MOS Hub. Drivers are distributed as plugins, and some plugins add their own page to the WebUI.
- **Pool**: One or more disks managed together as a single storage area. MOS supports single, multi, mergerfs, nonraid and bcachefs pools, plus Virtual Pools built from existing paths.
- **PWA**: A website that can be installed as an app. MOS Docs can be installed and cached for offline reading.
- **RAID**: Combining several disks into one protected volume. MOS multi pools support RAID 0 (striping, no protection) and RAID 1 (mirroring).
- **Rate limit**: Protection that caps API requests at 20 per second by default. The defaults are tuned for stability and should not be changed.
- **Resync**: Rebuilding parity, or rebuilding a replaced data disk from parity. A nonraid pool is usable during the initial resync but not yet protected.
- **samba_only**: A user role without WebUI access. The account can only authenticate against file shares.
- **Scrub**: A maintenance task that reads all data and verifies it against stored checksums, repairing from a mirror where possible. Available for btrfs and bcachefs.
- **Share**: A folder on a pool that is shared over SMB or NFS.
- **SMB**: The Windows file-sharing protocol. MOS provides SMB shares through Samba.
- **SMART**: Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology. Disk health data used for warnings and temperature limits.
- **SnapRAID**: Parity-based protection for mergerfs pools. It is not a live RAID; parity is updated on a schedule.
- **Snapshot**: A point-in-time copy of a container or VM disk used for backups and rollback. LXC snapshot backups require btrfs storage; VM snapshots require qcow2 disks.
- **Spindown**: Putting idle disks into standby after a configured number of minutes to save power and reduce noise.
- **Swapfile**: A file on disk used as virtual memory when physical RAM is exhausted. Configured under Settings > System Configuration > System.
- **Tailscale**: A WireGuard-based mesh VPN that gives remote access to MOS without port forwarding.
- **Update channel**: The firmware track MOS follows: alpha (team testing only), beta (pre-release) or stable (recommended for production).
- **UPS**: A battery backup that keeps the server running during a power outage. MOS monitors it through NUT and can shut down gracefully.
- **Virtual Pool**: A pool built from existing directory paths (for example /mnt/main and /mnt/media) combined with mergerfs. No dedicated disks and no formatting required.
- **VirtIO**: Paravirtualized disk and network drivers for virtual machines. They offer the best performance and need separate drivers inside Windows guests.
- **VLAN**: A tagged (802.1Q) network segment configured on an interface. A VLAN can carry its own IP or be used only for bridging.
- **WebUI**: The MOS browser interface. It performs no direct system actions; every action goes through the MOS API.
- **XFS**: A journaling filesystem recommended for mergerfs and nonraid data disks.
- **ZFS**: A copy-on-write filesystem with snapshots, checksums and RAID-Z. Available through the OpenZFS Driver plugin and currently CLI only.
- **ZRAM**: A compressed block device in RAM used as compressed swap or as a fast RAM disk.
- **Zswap**: A kernel feature that compresses memory pages in RAM before they are written to swap.
